sentences.text:
(Presently lodged in District Jail, Pali).
 ----Petitioner  Versus State of Rajasthan, through P.P.
 ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Tirath Raj Singh Sodha For Respondent(s) : Mr. Laxman Solanki, P.P.
For Complainant : Mr. Dilip Singh Rathore  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 10/08/2023

This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.187/2021 registered at Police Station Transport Nagar, District Pali for the offences under Sections 498A, 406, 506, 323 and 306 IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Transport Nagar, District Pali
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per prosecution, on 15.12.2021, deceased- Smt. Jyoti ended her life by jumping before a moving train.

Before committing suicide, she had written a suicide note, stating therein that, she is committing suicide owing to the abusive behaviour of his husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law,
sister-in-law, brother- in-law (nandoi) i.e. present petitioner, elder brother of his husband and his wife.

In the suicide note, it was alleged that her (2 of 6) [CRLMB-9712/2023] in-laws forcibly took away her minor children namely Nidhi and Parikshit and sent them to the house of present petitioner (nandoi), and since, she cannot live without her children, she is committing suicide.
As per prosecution, the marriage of the deceased was solemnised with Raghu Raj Singh, son of Shambhu Singh on 26.02.2009, as per Hindu rites and rituals.
The family members of the deceased to the best of their capability gave dowry in the marriage.
However, her in-laws were not happy and satisfied with the dowry received and therefore, they including present petitioner used to harrass her for demand of dowry.

The deceased gave birth to two children namely Nidhi and Parikshit, in Niranjan Singh vs State Of Rajasthan on 10 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183080968/
1 the year 2010 and 2013 respectively, and at that time also, gold and silver ornaments were given to the in laws of deceased as gifts.

sentences.text: As per prosecution, the husband of the deceased was also having extra marital affair.

Owing to aforesaid facts, the deceased left her matrimonial house, however, on receiving assurance from in-laws that they will not maltreat her in future, she returned to her matrimonial house in 2015.
In the year 2018, deceased again got pregnant, however, she was made to consume abortion pills.
As per prosecution, the deceased due to the bad behaviour of her in-laws returned to her parental house, from where her children were forcibly taken by the accused persons on 26.11.2021.

Deceased in these circumstances on 10.12.2021 submitted a written complaint before Superintendent of Police stating inter alia that she has been meted out with physical and mental cruelty by the accused persons.

Counselling/ Mediation (3 of 6) [CRLMB-9712/2023] proceedings were thereafter,
conducted by the relatives wherein, in-laws of the deceased flatly refused to return the children.

In a nutshell, the allegation against the present petitioner, who is brother-in-law (nandoi) of the deceased is that he along with his in-laws played an active role in terrorising and harassing the deceased in connection with dowry demand through his abusive behaviour towards her.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Learned counsel submitted that the marriage of the deceased was solemnised with co-accused Raghuveer Singh on 26.02.2009.

It was urged that the petitioner who is a government servant and admittedly living separately from the deceased and her in-laws could not have played any active role in demand of dowry or in the commission of alleged crime.

Learned counsel submitted that even if, for the sake of argument, it is accepted that the deceased was meted out with cruelty or subjected to dowry demand for twelve years by her in laws, then also she should have taken recourse to the remedies available to her under various laws, instead of ending her life by committing suicide.

Learned counsel submitted that in the suicide note, though, the author of the letter has levelled allegations of abusive behaviour against her in laws including petitioner but the same is not indicative of any active action on the part of the present petitioner to instigate, aid or abet the deceased to commit suicide.

Learned counsel submitted that unless the ingredients of instigation/abetment to commit suicide are satisfied, the accused (4 of 6) [CRLMB-9712/2023]
cannot be charged for offences under Section 306 IPC.

It was thus submitted that the petitioner's conduct cannot be said to be of such nature which would drive/ likely to drive the deceased to commit suicide Lastly, learned counsel submitted that challan against the present petitioner has already been filed before competent criminal court by the investigating agency on 16.09.2022, and no recovery is due to be made from present petitioner; whether or not the petitioner pressurised the deceased to bring more dowry or not would be decided by the trial court based on the testimonies and evidence led before it.
On the strength of these submissions, learned counsel implored the Court to grant indulgence of bail to the present petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail application and jointly submitted that sufficient evidence is available on record to indicate that behaviour of the petitioner was cruel towards the deceased and she was subjected to dowry demands.

Learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that misdeeds and abusive behaviour of the petitioner and other accused persons left the deceased with no other option except to commit suicide.

Learned counsel submitted that soon before committing suicide,
the deceased submitted a written complaint before Superintendent of Police and she had also left a suicide note, levelling serious allegations against the present petitioner and other accused persons,
which drove her to commit suicide.
(5 of 6) [CRLMB-9712/2023] It was thus, prayed that looking to the seriousness of allegations against the petitioner, he may not be granted concession of bail in the present case.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

Having considered rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case so also challan papers and documents annexed to it, this Court prima facie finds that serious allegations have been levelled against the present petitioner in connection with dowry demand and abusive behaviour/cruelty towards deceased.

However, whether the deceased was abetted or instigated to commit suicide for her failure to satisfy dowry demands or whether the petitioner by his acts or omissions or by continued course of conduct created such an atmosphere that the deceased was left with no option but to commit suicide, is a matter to be examined by the competent criminal court after conducting regular trial against the present petitioner.
Any comment on this aspect of the matter by this Court would definitely prejudice the trial pending against the present petitioner.
This Court without expressing any opinion upon the merits or demerits of the case, deems it just and proper to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner - Niranjan Singh S/o Sh. Chandan Singh arrested in connection with F.I.R.
No.187/2021 registered at Police Station Transport Nagar, District Pali shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, (6 of 6) [CRLMB-9712/2023] provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.

sentences.text: It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.
